title: ～けど — casual “but / although”
summary: A conjunction that follows a statement with something contrasting. It attaches to plain forms and is common in conversation. For polite situations use が or けれども.

patterns.form: 名詞・な形容詞＋だけど

body.p: It joins two clauses and shows contrast: 安いけど、おいしいです.

body.h: Ending a sentence with けど
body.p: In conversation けど can end a sentence, leaving the rest unsaid, which softens it (すみませんけど…).

body.h: Difference from けれども and が
body.p: All three show contrast. けど is the most casual, then けれど and けれども, and が is the most formal.

examples.ja: 行（い）きたいけど、時間（じかん）がありません。
examples.tr: I want to go, but I don't have time.

examples.ja: 安（やす）いけど、おいしいです。
暑（あつ）いけど、外（そと）で遊（あそ）びます。
examples.tr: It's hot, but I'll play outside.

pitfalls: Japanese uses just one けど. There is no need for a pair like “although... but...”.
In formal situations avoid けど and use が or けれども.
